topics.title: 隐私与敏感数据
topics.summary: Yale's September 2023 Provost guidance says not to enter confidential, legally restricted, Moderate-risk or High-risk Yale data into an AI tool. The current institutional directory separately lists service-specific data classifications, including Clarity for High-risk data with special ePHI and DUA conditions, while Radiate web search is limited to Low-risk data. Follow the service's access restrictions and applicable data agreements; these classifications do not settle authorization for every dataset.

claims.text: Yale's September2023 Provost guidance says not to enter confidential, legally restricted, moderate-risk or high-risk Yale data into an AI tool. additionalTopics.summary: Inserting AI-generated content into submitted work without proper attribution constitutes an academic integrity violation. Under GSAS 2026–2027 standards, graduate students must consult relevant faculty before using AI in coursework or research and must be prepared to articulate and demonstrate their drafting process if requested, but there is no universal requirement for all students to log every prompt. Disciplinary responses are managed by the Committee on Regulations and Discipline; written student statements are ordinarily due within two weeks.

Hearings are conducted by a panel of at least four members (including a usually non-voting secretary; three voting members including at least one student form a quorum). Decisions are made by secret ballot on a preponderance of the evidence; the committee recommends a sanction to the dean, who determines the penalty. Disciplinary decisions take immediate effect. Students may submit a written appeal to the Committee of Review no later than five business days after the committee decision. The Committee of Review (three members) may decline action or request reconsideration; on reconsideration, the committee cannot find culpability if previously exonerated or impose a more severe penalty. Scope is restricted to GSAS; research misconduct is referred under Research Misconduct procedures; undergraduate cases follow separate Yale College Executive Committee procedures.

evidence.quote: Student statement. Students will be asked to respond in writing to the allegation. Providing a written statement allows the student to present their perspective on events and any broader context or other information that will help the Coordinating Group and committee to better understand the situation. Written statements will ordinarily be due to the secretary two weeks after the student receives notification of the charge. In their statement, students should admit or deny allegations against them. In some cases, the student may admit responsibility for some portion of the allegations and deny others.

evidence.quote: A hearing panel will have a minimum of four members, including the secretary (or dean’s designate) who does not typically vote. Voting members of the panel must include the chair or vice chair, one faculty member and/or dean of the graduate school, and one student member. The presence of three voting members will constitute a quorum, provided that at least one student member is present. A majority vote will decide questions before the hearing panel. In the event of a tie vote, the secretary or other committee designee will cast a deciding vote.

evidence.quote: Determination. At the conclusion of the hearing, the committee will meet in an executive session to decide whether the conduct reported in fact occurred and whether it contravened the standards cited in the charge. The committee’s decision will be made by a simple majority of voting members present. The secretary will vote only in the event of a tie. This decision will be made by a preponderance of the evidence, voted on by secret ballot, and will be final.
